name: Ferro Colorblock Hoodie
description:
A pullover hoodie in a bold colorblock design — the body is a deep rust-orange and the sleeves are near-black, with a horizontal seam across the chest where the two panels meet. The hood is oversized and unlined, the kind you can actually pull down over your face. The kangaroo pocket is deep. The fabric is a mid-weight fleece-backed synth-cotton that's soft on the inside and slightly textured on the outside, with just enough weight to feel substantial without restricting movement.

Ferro is a street brand from the Chicago-side of the corridor, started by two siblings who began selling out of a converted storage unit. They're now in three brick-and-mortar shops and an online catalog, but the aesthetic hasn't changed — loud color, honest construction, no pretense. The Ferro tag on the inside of the neck has a small embossed lightning bolt. Fakes exist but the emboss is hard to replicate cleanly.
what_it_says: You buy from people, not corporations. You like color. You're comfortable taking up space.
worn_by: people who want style at an honest price
story_hooks: Ferro has been approached by a corponation interested in a 'collaboration' — the siblings are split on whether to take the money and the exposure or protect what they've built.
The rust-orange and black colorway has been adopted by a specific crew in the Shelf as their colors — which is creating problems for people who wear it without affiliation.
A character spots someone they've been looking for based entirely on the distinctive colorblock pattern visible at the edge of a crowd.

physical_description.visual_profile: A striking colorblock pullover that reads as deliberately bold without trying too hard. The rust-orange torso contrasts sharply with near-black sleeves, creating a visual weight that draws the eye to the chest and shoulders. The oversized hood dominates the silhouette when pulled up, framing the face with an almost protective quality. Worn relaxed and low-slung on the body, it has the confident asymmetry of street-wear that knows what it is.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and intentionally oversized through the body and shoulders, with sleeves that taper slightly at the wrist but remain slouchy. The hood is generously cut and drops well past the shoulders when worn up. The overall cut prioritizes movement and layering compatibility over fitted tailoring.
physical_description.primary_material: Mid-weight fleece-backed synth-cotton blend — durable and temperature-regulating without the brittleness of pure synthetic fabrics
physical_description.texture: Soft brushed interior with a subtle nap; exterior has a slight texture created by the cotton-synthetic weave, giving it visual depth and preventing it from looking flat or cheap
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep rust-orange (almost burnt sienna) across the body; near-black (charcoal-weighted) on both sleeves. A clean horizontal seam at chest height marks the color transition. No additional trim or contrast stitching — the colorblock is the design statement.
physical_description.closures: Pullover style; no zippers or buttons. The kangaroo pocket is simple and unadorned, with a relaxed opening
distinctive_features: Bold colorblock construction — intentional, not accidental
Oversized unlined hood that can fully obscure the face when pulled down
Deep kangaroo pocket suitable for large objects (tools, devices, hands)
Clean horizontal seam at chest marking the two-panel construction
Small embossed lightning bolt on the interior neck tag (Ferro's signature detail, difficult to counterfeit cleanly)
Honest construction visible in seam work — no hidden overlocking or glossy finishing
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional aesthetic with street credibility. Not luxury, not salvage — deliberate and made-to-last
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals independent street culture, Chicago-corridor affiliation, and a wearer who values honest design over corporate branding. Worn by technicians, courier riders, street artists, and working-class augment-modders who recognize quality construction and aren't trying to perform wealth they don't have
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in rather than pristine. After a few months of wear, the exterior develops a subtle patina from handling, the pocket edges show character, and the fabric softens further. Rarely looks new, but rarely looks neglected — it's made to be used
